item.title: When Can You Play GTA VI? The Full Release Timeline
item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI launches Thursday, November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. But it does not unlock everywhere at once. The game rolls out region by region, at midnight local time…
item.content:encoded:
When Can You Play GTA VI? The Full Release Timeline

Grand Theft Auto VI launches Thursday, November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. But it does not unlock everywhere at once. The game rolls out region by region, at midnight local time in each store region, in 15 waves over 19 hours.

New Zealand plays first — 11:00am UTC on Wednesday, November 18 (6:00am Eastern). From there it sweeps across Australia, Japan, Europe, South America, and finally the Americas. Mexico and Central America play last — 6:00am UTC on November 19 (1:00am Eastern).

For us on the East Coast: midnight Eastern, Thursday, November 19. That is 11:00pm Central, 10:00pm Mountain, and 9:00pm Pacific on Wednesday night. The whole United States unlocks at once, because the stores carry one timestamp per country.

One more date to know: pre-load starts Tuesday, November 10, and the download is up to 212 gigabytes. Clear the space now so you are ready the second the clock hits midnight.

Geeked walks through the full timeline in the video below, and Nova breaks it all down in her own episode of The Nerds List Daily.

Watch the video: GTA VI — When Can You Play? (YouTube Short)
See it on Instagram: The timeline, on @thenerdslist

These times come from the PlayStation Store and Xbox Store listings, and they can still change before launch. Rockstar has confirmed the date, not the hour. We will update this post if anything moves.

— Geeked & Nova, The Nerd's List

item.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Sells 5.2 Million Copies in Four Days — a Switch 2 Record
item.description: The Ocarina of Time. 3D render by PantheraLeo1359531, Wikimedia Commons (CC0). The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has sold more than 5.2 million copies worldwide in its first four days,…
item.content:encoded:
The Ocarina of Time. 3D render by PantheraLeo1359531, Wikimedia Commons (CC0).

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has sold more than 5.2 million copies worldwide in its first four days, Nintendo announced — the biggest four-day launch for any Nintendo-published Switch 2 game ever.

The Switch 2 exclusive launched on November 5, 2026, and by the end of November 9 it had already become the second-best-selling Switch 2 game, trailing only Mario Kart World. Nintendo says the 5.2 million figure covers physical and digital sales combined, including 810,000 copies in Japan.

Nintendo Switch 2 in its dock. Photo by Crisco 1492, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0).

Here is why the number is so staggering:

  • A record launch: Nintendo calls it the highest global sales for any Nintendo-published Switch 2 game in its first four days — ahead of Donkey Kong Bananza (5.05 million) and Pokémon Pokopia (5.18 million).
  • One in five Switch 2 owners bought it: with roughly 26.35 million Switch 2 consoles in players' hands, the remake has about a 20 percent attach rate after four days.
  • Already a top-ten Zelda: in less than a week, the remake is the eighth best-selling game in the series' history, passing Phantom Hourglass (4.76 million) and closing in on the 3DS version of Ocarina of Time itself (6.44 million).
  • Critics agree: the remake sits at 96 on Metacritic, making it one of the best-reviewed games of the year.

The remake is a full rebuild of the 1998 Nintendo 64 classic, with overhauled visuals, orchestral music, voice acting, and expanded cutscenes, and it sells for $59.99 physically or $49.99 digitally. We reviewed it here at The Nerd's List on November 8 — and the sales suggest plenty of players agreed with the verdict.

The timing is no accident: Zelda is having a moment. The franchise turns 40 this year, and the first-ever live-action Zelda film is set to hit theaters on April 30, 2027. A remake this big, this fast, shows the appetite for Hyrule is nowhere near fading — and with the holiday season ahead, 5.2 million is almost certainly just the start.

Source: Nintendo press release, via Polygon, VGC, Gematsu, and Shacknews.

item.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping — Haymitch's Games Hit Theaters November 20
item.description: Panem is calling us back to the arena — and this time, the story belongs to the mentor we thought we already knew. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping hits theaters on Friday, November 20, 2026…
item.content:encoded:
Panem is calling us back to the arena — and this time, the story belongs to the mentor we thought we already knew. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping hits theaters on Friday, November 20, 2026, and it is shaping up to be the biggest event movie of the month. Early premium-format screenings begin Wednesday, November 18, so the truly impatient among us do not have to wait the full ten days.

The film takes us 24 years before Katniss Everdeen, to the morning of the reaping for the 50th Hunger Games — the Second Quarter Quell. To mark the occasion, the Capitol doubles the tribute count: 48 young fighters enter the arena instead of the usual 24. At the center of it all is a 16-year-old Haymitch Abernathy, played by newcomer Joseph Zada — the same scrappy District 12 kid who will grow up to become the sharp-tongued, bottle-in-hand mentor Woody Harrelson made iconic in the first four films.

Director Francis Lawrence is back behind the camera for his fifth Hunger Games film, having directed every entry since Catching Fire. The screenplay comes from Billy Ray and Michael Lesslie, adapting Suzanne Collins's novel, which was published on March 18, 2025. James Newton Howard returns to score the film, as he has for every Hunger Games movie so far.

And what a cast it is. Mckenna Grace plays fellow District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner, and Whitney Peak plays Haymitch's love, Lenore Dove Baird. The Capitol side of the story is stacked too: Ralph Fiennes steps in as President Coriolanus Snow, Elle Fanning plays a young Effie Trinket, Jesse Plemons is a young Plutarch Heavensbee, and Kieran Culkin takes on Caesar Flickerman. Maya Hawke appears as Wiress and Kelvin Harrison Jr. as Beetee, with Glenn Close rounding out the ensemble.

Then there is the reunion fans have been waiting over a decade for. At the film's London premiere on October 28, Jennifer Lawrence confirmed that she, Josh Hutcherson, and Woody Harrelson all return — Katniss, Peeta, and the older Haymitch, back on screen together for the first time in 11 years. First reactions out of that premiere have been glowing, with particular praise for Zada's Haymitch.

The numbers say the hype is real. Boxoffice Pro estimates a $55–65 million opening weekend, which would clear the $44.6 million opening of the previous installment, 2023's The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes. At a listed 158 minutes and rated PG-13, this is the longest Hunger Games film yet — and, fittingly, the biggest Games ever put on screen.

So mark the calendar: November 20, in theaters and IMAX. Whether you have read Collins's novel cover to cover or you are walking in cold, this is a story that stands on its own — a teenager from District 12, a rigged arena, and a sunrise that changes everything. May the odds be ever in your favor.

Images: original illustrations created for The Nerd's List.

item.title: PlayStation Cancels Fairgames After Failed Playtests, Bloomberg Reports
item.description: PlayStation has cancelled Fairgames , the live-service heist shooter from Haven Studios, according to a Bloomberg report published today, November 10, 2026. The game — announced in 2023 and never…
item.content:encoded:
PlayStation has cancelled Fairgames, the live-service heist shooter from Haven Studios, according to a Bloomberg report published today, November 10, 2026. The game — announced in 2023 and never shown in full gameplay — is done, three years after its reveal.

Bloomberg reports that PlayStation made the call after the results of a recent playtest fell short. An internal note from PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle, verified by Bloomberg, put it bluntly: "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set. Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."

Haven Studios is not closing. PlayStation told Bloomberg there will be no layoffs as a result of the cancellation. Instead, the studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities. What Haven works on next has not been announced.

What Fairgames was

  • Revealed on May 24, 2023, at the PlayStation Showcase, as a competitive heist game where players join an underground movement to rob the ultra-rich
  • In development for PlayStation 5 and PC at Haven Studios, the Montreal studio founded by Jade Raymond in 2021 and acquired by Sony in 2022
  • Shown only in cinematic trailers since its reveal — footage that appeared to come from a playtest seemingly leaked online in September 2026, the first gameplay anyone had seen
  • Raymond left Haven in 2025 while development continued, after earlier reports that external playtests had been poorly received and the game had slipped to 2026

Why this matters

Fairgames was one of the flagship titles of PlayStation's big live-service push, and its cancellation is the latest setback in that strategy. Concord flopped so badly that PlayStation pulled it from sale and shut down developer Firewalk Studios. Helldivers 2 remains the one clear success from that era, and Bungie is still working to grow Marathon's player base. Sony has said live-service games remain an important part of PlayStation's future — but it clearly does not want to add another struggling multiplayer shooter to the mix right now.

PlayStation has not publicly commented on the cancellation on its own channels yet — the news is known so far through Bloomberg's report and the internal email. For players, the practical result is simple: there is no Fairgames release to look forward to, because the game never launched. For Haven, the question now is what the studio builds next — and whether PlayStation's live-service era has any big bets left at all. Photo: a PlayStation 5 console with DualSense controller, by Howardcorn33 via Wikimedia Commons (CC0, public domain).

item.title: Amazon's Ring Drone Cam Is a Flying Security Camera — and It Ships in January
item.description: Your next security camera might not sit on a shelf — it might fly around your house . Amazon announced on November 10, 2026 that Ring is moving beyond doorbells with two new AI-powered security…
item.content:encoded:
Your next security camera might not sit on a shelf — it might fly around your house. Amazon announced on November 10, 2026 that Ring is moving beyond doorbells with two new AI-powered security robots: the Ring Drone Cam, a flying indoor camera for your home, and the Ring Rover Cam, an autonomous patrol robot built for businesses. Yes, your smart home is about to get a tiny air force.

The star of the show is the Drone Cam. It's a small indoor drone that lives in a dock with its camera off when it's not working — no awkward staring lens while you're eating dinner. When it's time for a check-in, you can send it flying on custom routes and schedules you set, or deploy it on demand. And if one of your other Ring cameras, sensors, or alarms gets triggered, the drone automatically flies over to investigate on its own. That's the kind of thing that used to be pure sci-fi, and now it's a product you can buy.

The specs are no joke either. The Drone Cam captures 2K video with a 148-degree field of view and can rotate a full 365 degrees, so it can sweep a whole room from a single hover. Two LED lights switch on automatically in low light — and they also make it obvious when the drone is in use, so nobody's wondering whether it's recording. It costs $249.99 and begins shipping in the United States on January 27, 2027. You can sign up for email updates on Amazon's website to be notified when it's available.

Its bigger sibling, the Ring Rover Cam, is aimed at businesses rather than living rooms. It's a wheeled robot that can run scheduled sweeps before opening or after closing, or roll over to check out a disturbance. It records in up to 4K video, packs a built-in siren and light tower, two-way audio so you can speak through it, and a periscope camera that pops up for a better view. The Rover costs $999.99, is available to preorder now, and ships in the United States on December 16, 2026.

Both devices run on AI Pilot, Amazon's custom-built system that uses each device's cameras, vision models, sensors, and cloud processing to see, think, and navigate on its own. Setup is charmingly simple: carry the Drone through your space once, or let the Rover explore by itself, and each device turns what it sees into a digital floor plan it can navigate later.

Is a flying camera the future of home security, or just the coolest gadget of the year? Either way, Ring just made the smart home a lot more interesting — and a lot more airborne. We'll be watching to see how it handles real homes, pets, and the occasional ceiling fan.

Source: USA TODAY, "Ring expands beyond doorbells with new flying security camera," reporting on Amazon's November 10, 2026 announcement. Images in this post are original illustrations created for The Nerd's List.

item.title: GTA VI Will Run at 30 FPS on Consoles — Rockstar Confirms, No Performance Mode Announced
item.description: Rockstar has finally answered the question every GTA fan has been asking: how will Grand Theft Auto VI run? The answer, confirmed in a Rockstar Newswire post today, November 10, 2026: 30 frames per…
item.content:encoded:
Rockstar has finally answered the question every GTA fan has been asking: how will Grand Theft Auto VI run? The answer, confirmed in a Rockstar Newswire post today, November 10, 2026: 30 frames per second on every console — PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and even the PlayStation 5 Pro. The post names no 60fps performance mode.

Rockstar says GTA VI was built "from the ground up" for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30fps while pushing both platforms "to their absolute limits" to bring the world of Leonida to life — while maintaining the density and visual fidelity of its environments and inhabitants. In other words, Rockstar chose a denser, richer Vice City over a higher frame rate, and the studio is not promising a smoother option at launch.

What PS5 Pro owners actually get

  • PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) for a sharper image
  • Ray-traced shadows available only on PS5 Pro
  • No higher frame-rate target — Pro owners get a better-looking game, not a smoother one

Base PS5 players still get the platform's full feature set: faster load times from the SSD, Tempest 3D Audio, and DualSense haptic feedback. Rockstar says the game "plays best" on PlayStation 5 — a line that echoes Sony's marketing, and unsurprising given the two companies' marketing deal.

Xbox players get something PlayStation doesn't

GTA VI will be playable through Xbox Cloud Gaming on Xbox Series X|S and Xbox One, using Xbox Series S settings — so even last-gen Xbox One owners can play on launch day via the cloud. Streaming begins at 10:00pm Pacific on November 18 (1:00am Eastern on November 19). Remote Play is supported on both PlayStation and Xbox.

Pre-loads are live right now

Digital pre-orders can pre-load today on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, with boxed-copy buyers able to pre-load as soon as they receive their download code. The pre-load runs up to 212GB depending on the device. The game unlocks at midnight local time on November 19, 2026.

The demand is already historic. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said on yesterday's earnings call that pre-orders are exceeding the publisher's already lofty expectations, and Sony and Xbox say GTA VI is the most preordered game ever on their stores.

Nine days out, the picture is finally complete: 30fps everywhere, a prettier Pro, cloud play on Xbox One, and a launch that is shaping up to be the biggest in gaming history. Photo: the Miami skyline — the real-world inspiration for Vice City — via Wikimedia Commons (CC0).

item.title: GTA VI Launches November 19 — The Countdown Is On
item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI launches November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, and the countdown is officially on. With pre-loads now live, players can start downloading the game ahead of…
item.content:encoded:
Grand Theft Auto VI launches November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, and the countdown is officially on. With pre-loads now live, players can start downloading the game ahead of launch day and be ready to step into Vice City the moment it unlocks.

Rockstar's return to Vice City has been the most anticipated launch in gaming for years, and the final stretch is here. The game arrives nine days after pre-loads opened, giving players time to get the download done before launch morning.

Here's what you need to know:

  • Launch date: Thursday, November 19, 2026
  • Platforms: PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S
  • Pre-loads: Live now — download ahead of launch day
  • Setting: Vice City and the state of Leonida

Vice City is Rockstar's neon-soaked Florida-inspired playground, and GTA VI brings it back bigger than ever, with Lucia and Jason at the center of the story. The game has dominated conversation since its first trailer, and every new detail — from the map to the music — has only raised the stakes.

Launch week is packed beyond the game itself. GTA VI: The Album arrives on launch day, and Rockstar's one-night live music event, Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival, takes over Miami on Saturday, November 21 — two days after launch.

Watch the countdown: YouTube Short • Instagram Reel

Launch timing matters if you want to be in Vice City first. In the United States, the game unlocks at midnight Eastern on November 19, so the earliest players will be in on the dot. Pre-loads are up to 212 GB, so clear the space now rather than on launch night — the download is one of the biggest in console history, and nobody wants to be staring at a progress bar while everyone else is already driving down Ocean Drive.

While you wait, The Nerd's List Daily is covering GTA VI launch week every morning at 5:00am ET — the review, the tips, and everything Rockstar drops next. Keep it locked to thenerdslist.com for the full countdown.

item.title: SPY×FAMILY Season 4 and a New Movie Are Coming in 2027
item.description: The Forger family is coming back — twice over. On Sunday, November 8, the staff behind SPY×FAMILY announced that the anime is getting a fourth season and a brand-new theatrical film, both arriving in…
item.content:encoded:
The Forger family is coming back — twice over. On Sunday, November 8, the staff behind SPY×FAMILY announced that the anime is getting a fourth season and a brand-new theatrical film, both arriving in 2027. A fresh visual for Season 4 dropped alongside the announcement, and the fandom has been buzzing ever since.

Let's be real: this is exactly the kind of double announcement that makes anime fans lose their minds. Season 3 only just wrapped its run after premiering in October 2025 with 13 episodes, and the team is already locking in the next chapter — plus a trip back to the big screen. No exact dates have been confirmed yet for either the season or the film, so keep your calendars penciled in, not inked.

A quick refresher on how we got here:

  • Season 1 premiered in April 2022, with its second half following in October 2022.
  • Season 2 premiered in October 2023 and ran for 12 episodes.
  • Season 3 premiered in October 2025 with 13 episodes.
  • The first film, SPY×FAMILY Code: White, opened in Japan in December 2023, topped the Japanese box office in its opening weekend, and reached North American theaters via Crunchyroll in April 2024 — with an all-original story.

Underneath it all is Tatsuya Endō's manga, which launched on Shonen Jump+ in March 2019 and just published its 18th compiled volume on November 4. Viz Media publishes the manga in English, and Shueisha releases it simultaneously in English on MANGA Plus — so whether you read or watch, there is plenty of Forger family to catch up on while we wait.

What makes SPY×FAMILY so special is that it somehow nails every genre at once: a master spy, an assassin wife, a telepathic daughter, and a dog who can see the future, all pretending to be the most normal family in Ostania. It is a spy thriller, a comedy, and a found-family heart-warmer rolled into one — and it has stayed that way across three seasons without losing a step.

With a fourth season and a second film both on the way in 2027, next year is shaping up to be a huge one for Loid, Yor, Anya, and Bond. We will be covering every trailer, date reveal, and detail as it lands — and Nova is diving into the announcement on The Nerds List Daily this Thursday, November 12, with a special episode all about what Season 4 could mean. Stay tuned, and keep an eye out for peanuts.

item.title: GTA VI Has Gone Gold — Pre-Loads Are Live, Launch Locked for November 19
item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI is done. Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick confirmed on the company's earnings call on Monday, November 9, that Rockstar Games has completed development on GTA VI — the…
item.content:encoded:
Grand Theft Auto VI is done. Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick confirmed on the company's earnings call on Monday, November 9, that Rockstar Games has completed development on GTA VI — the game has gone gold, locking in its November 19, 2026 launch on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

"Right now, Rockstar has completed the development of GTA VI," Zelnick told investors, ten days before launch. Pre-orders, he added, are "tracking far in excess of our initial expectations," with Take-Two describing demand as reaching unprecedented levels. The road here was long: GTA VI was first scheduled for late 2025, then pushed to May 26, 2026, before landing on its current November 19 date — and this time, there is no further delay in sight.

Going gold means the launch build is finished and locked. It does not mean Rockstar's work is over — a day-one patch is still possible, as with most major releases — but the version that ships is set, and the countdown to launch night is now a matter of days, not months.

You do not have to wait until launch night to download it, either. Pre-loading is live right now for digital pre-orders:

  • PlayStation 5: pre-load opens at midnight local time on Tuesday, November 10.
  • Xbox Series X|S: pre-load opened globally at 12 a.m. GMT on November 10 — 7 p.m. Eastern on Monday, November 9.
  • Space needed: Rockstar's pre-load FAQ says to clear up to 212 GB of available space, depending on your device — so free up room before you start.
  • Unlock: the game stays locked until midnight local time on November 19. Downloading early saves you from a launch-night wait, not from the wait itself.

One thing to know before you head to the store: boxed copies of GTA VI contain a download code rather than a disc, and they go on sale from November 12. Once you redeem the code, you can pre-load from then.

The game returns to Vice City, in the state of Leonida, following Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval after a failed heist pulls them into a state-wide conspiracy. Rockstar is also celebrating launch week in the real world: GTA VI: The Festival takes over Miami on Saturday, November 21, two days after launch.

Nine days out, the biggest launch in gaming history is officially real, finished, and already landing on hard drives. Clear the space, start the download, and we will see you in Vice City on November 19.

item.title: James Gunn and Peter Safran Are Out at DC Studios — Marvel Veteran Jeremy Latcham Takes Over
item.description: James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as the co-heads of DC Studios, and a Marvel veteran is taking over the DC Universe. Skydance announced the stunning shake-up on Monday, November 9, 2026,…
item.content:encoded:
James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as the co-heads of DC Studios, and a Marvel veteran is taking over the DC Universe. Skydance announced the stunning shake-up on Monday, November 9, 2026, ending the duo's four-year run in charge of DC's film, television, and animation slate.

Former Marvel Studios executive Jeremy Latcham will take over as president and chief creative officer of DC Studios, effective December 1. Latcham, who served as Marvel's senior vice president of production and development, has credits on Iron Man, The Avengers, Guardians of the Galaxy, and the Spider-Man films. He will report to Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein, co-chairs of the Skydance Motion Picture Group.

Gunn and Safran were hired in 2022 to reboot DC's screen universe under one creative vision. Their tenure delivered the new DC Universe's first chapter, including the 2025 Superman relaunch, which grossed $618 million worldwide, plus the series Peacemaker, Creature Commandos, and Lanterns.

The pair are not leaving DC entirely. In a joint statement, Gunn and Safran said they are returning to full-time creative work, and Gunn confirmed on social media that he is still working on Man of Tomorrow, the Superman follow-up now in post-production for summer 2027, plus another DC project he is writing.

"Four years ago, we set out to unite DC under one creative vision," the pair said in their statement. "We're excited to return to what drew us to this job in the first place, which is telling the stories we love, including the next chapter of Clark and Lex's journey in Man of Tomorrow."

The move comes just weeks after Skydance completed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on October 6. Gunn and Safran had initially stayed on through the merger, but Skydance CEO David Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz praised the duo's work while announcing the transition, saying they "helped restore Superman to the heart of DC."

What happens next is the big question:

  • Does the DCU continue or reboot? With Man of Tomorrow due July 9, 2027, and The Batman: Part II slated for 2028, Latcham inherits a slate already in motion — but no DCU film is currently in production.
  • Where do Gunn and Safran land? Gunn says he is engaged on another DC project beyond Man of Tomorrow — and "we'll see where it goes after that."
  • What does Latcham change? A Marvel veteran running DC is a twist nobody saw coming, and his first calls on the slate will set the tone for the next era.

For now, the DC Universe has a new boss, and the nerd world will be watching every move he makes.
item.dc:creator: Jamal Jarrett

item.title: SPY×FAMILY Is Coming Back Twice: Season 4 and a Second Movie Confirmed for 2027
item.description: The Forger family is officially coming back — twice . At the SPY×FAMILY ANIME EXTRA MISSION II special event in Tokyo on Sunday, November 8, the production team confirmed that SPY×FAMILY Season 4 is…
item.content:encoded:
The Forger family is officially coming back — twice. At the SPY×FAMILY ANIME EXTRA MISSION II special event in Tokyo on Sunday, November 8, the production team confirmed that SPY×FAMILY Season 4 is on the way, and that the franchise is also getting a second theatrical movie. Both projects are slated for 2027. A brand-new Season 4 teaser visual, drawn by character designer Satoshi Kadowaki, was unveiled alongside the announcement.

That is a double dose of good news for a series that has become one of the biggest anime success stories of the decade. The manga by Tatsuya Endo has been a hit since it launched on Shonen Jump+ in 2019, and the anime — produced by WIT STUDIO and CloverWorks — has kept that momentum going season after season. Season 1 premiered in April 2022 with 25 episodes, Season 2 followed in late 2023, and Season 3 aired from October to December 2025. Now the Forgers are locked in for another round on TV and on the big screen.

The first film, SPY×FAMILY CODE: White, opened in Japanese cinemas in December 2023 and proved the family could carry a movie, too. The second film follows in its footsteps — but here is the honest part: we do not know its title, its story, or its exact release date yet. The announcement likewise gave no premiere month or episode count for Season 4. Season 4 will be directed by Yasuhiro Akamatsu, with the original voice cast returning. Everything else is still under wraps, so treat any title or plot rumors floating around online as unconfirmed until the official site or TOHO Animation says otherwise.

So what should fans watch for next? The next big reveal window is Jump Festa on December 19–20, 2026, where the franchise could drop a premiere window, a trailer, or the film's title. Until then, the smartest move is a rewatch: all three seasons stream on Crunchyroll, and the wait for 2027 just got a whole lot more exciting.

And here is a fun bit of timing: our own Nova has a SPY×FAMILY special episode of The Nerds List Daily dropping this Thursday, November 12 at 8:00am ET — When Does SPY×FAMILY Season 4 Come Out? — and thanks to this weekend's announcement, we finally have the answer: 2027, with a movie on the way too. Loid, Yor, Anya, and Bond are coming home. We will be watching.

item.title: SEGA Confirms Data Breach: 2.2 Million Email Addresses Leaked
item.description: SEGA has confirmed a data breach that leaked the email addresses of 2,196,044 people who receive the company's newsletters. The company published the disclosure today, November 9, 2026, blaming a…
item.content:encoded:
SEGA has confirmed a data breach that leaked the email addresses of 2,196,044 people who receive the company's newsletters. The company published the disclosure today, November 9, 2026, blaming a third-party attack on Arara, the company that distributes SEGA's newsletters — and SEGA's breach is one slice of a much larger supply-chain attack that may have exposed as many as 81 million email addresses across hundreds of companies.

Here is what was taken, and what was not. The leaked data covers eleven newsletter batches sent between July 2 and October 28, 2026. SEGA says there is no indication that names, birthdates, genders, postal addresses, phone numbers, credit card information, or login passwords were leaked. People with a SEGA account are not affected — SEGA Accounts run on a separate system. One caveat: 92,273 of the leaked records also carried what SEGA calls "delivery-accompanying information," and SEGA and Arara are still verifying exactly what those rows contain.

The bigger picture is much larger than SEGA. Arara runs a bulk-email platform, and its investigation found that attackers reached 97 servers holding the mailing lists of up to roughly 380 client companies. Arara's third report, published November 6, raised the platform-wide total to 81,329,467 deduplicated email addresses. Attackers also used Arara's mail servers to send roughly 7.13 million fraudulent emails from a legitimate-looking sender address. Arara shut the whole platform down on October 31 and has not restarted it.

SEGA's arcade network was hit separately. On November 2, SEGA Fave reported unauthorized access to ALL.Net, the arcade network, and Aime player cards. SEGA stopped the network on November 1, taking games from SEGA and Bandai Namco dark in arcades across Japan, with no restart date yet. No data leak has been found so far in that incident, and SEGA says it is still investigating the cause.

What to do if you get SEGA newsletters. SEGA has suspended its newsletter distribution and says it will contact affected users individually once the details are confirmed. Until then, treat unexpected emails claiming to be from SEGA with suspicion — do not click links or attachments, and go to SEGA's official site directly to check anything. The leaked addresses are prime fuel for phishing, so make sure your passwords are unique, even though SEGA says none were exposed here.

This is the second major Japanese gaming breach in as many weeks: in late October, Capcom confirmed a similar incident affecting more than 11 million CAPCOM IDs. SEGA says it will strengthen how it handles personal data entrusted to outside providers and plans a joint report with Arara to Japan's privacy regulator.

More on this story as it develops at thenerdslist.com.

item.title: Geeked & Nova Are Boarding for Vice City — GTA VI Launch Countdown
item.description: Boarding passes: checked. Geeked and Nova are flying to Vice City. Their flyUS boarding passes are in hand for flight GT406 — Los Santos (LSX) to Vice City (VCI), departing Tuesday, November 18 at…
item.content:encoded:
Boarding passes: checked. Geeked and Nova are flying to Vice City.

Their flyUS boarding passes are in hand for flight GT406 — Los Santos (LSX) to Vice City (VCI), departing Tuesday, November 18 at 4:00 p.m. and touching down at midnight on Wednesday, November 19. Geeked is in seat 24G, Nova is right beside him in 24F, and the two of them are traveling together. Gate 6, Terminal 1. Destination: launch day.

Grand Theft Auto VI launches November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, and the countdown is officially on. Geeked and Nova already took you for a drive through Leonida in their 10-days-to-Vice-City promo — Lucia and Jason, the biggest GTA world ever, and a city ready to be explored.

Launch week is stacked. Nova's full GTA VI release-timeline episode drops Wednesday, November 11, covering the staggered midnight unlocks around the world. And Rockstar just announced GTA VI: The Festival — a one-night live music event in Miami on Saturday, November 21, two days after launch, with Travis Scott, Cardi B, Metro Boomin, Justice and more. The free ticket lottery for that one closes Tuesday, November 10 at 4:00 p.m. ET.

See both boarding passes on our Instagram — Geeked and Nova, seats 24G and 24F. Ten days to Vice City. Are you ready?

More on this story as it develops at thenerdslist.com.

item.title: Godzilla Minus Zero Just Smashed the North American Box Office — $31.6M and a New Record
item.description: The King is back — and this time he brought receipts. Godzilla Minus Zero just stomped its way to the top of the North American box office, earning an estimated $31.6 million in its opening weekend…
item.content:encoded:
The King is back — and this time he brought receipts. Godzilla Minus Zero just stomped its way to the top of the North American box office, earning an estimated $31.6 million in its opening weekend and setting a brand-new record: the biggest opening ever for a live-action foreign-language film in North America. Not bad for a monster who is 72 years old.

Directed by Takashi Yamazaki and produced by Toho, the film is the sequel to 2023's Oscar-winning Godzilla Minus One — and it is already outpacing its predecessor by a mile. Minus One opened to about $11.4 million in North America before finishing its run at roughly $57.1 million. Minus Zero nearly tripled that opening in a single weekend, and it has not even slowed down yet.

The worldwide picture is just as wild. The film has pulled in an estimated $63 million globally, including around $17 million in Japan, where it opened on November 3 to mark the franchise's 72nd anniversary. It opened in North America on November 6, distributed by GKIDS, and claimed the number one spot ahead of Warner Bros.' animated The Cat in the Hat, which debuted with $20.5 million.

Here is the part that makes Hollywood executives sweat: Godzilla Minus Zero reportedly cost less than $20 million to make. That is a fraction of what most blockbusters spend on catering, let alone CGI. Toho delivered a towering, terrifying kaiju epic on a budget that would barely cover a single action sequence in a typical superhero movie — and audiences rewarded it with the biggest opening weekend the franchise has ever seen in North America.

The story returns to post-World War II Japan, following the Shikishima family as they face a new catastrophe after their first encounter with the King of the Monsters. It is the same grounded, human-first approach that made Minus One a phenomenon: the monster is massive, but the movie never forgets the people running from him.

What does this mean for the rest of us? For starters, expect the conversation about what a blockbuster has to cost to get a whole lot louder. And if you have not seen it yet, get to a theater — this is the kind of movie that hits different with a crowd, a giant screen, and a theater full of people cheering every time that dorsal fin lights up.

Have you seen Godzilla Minus Zero yet? Tell us your favorite kaiju moment in the comments — and stay tuned to The Nerd's List for more box office shake-ups as the year winds down.

item.title: Rockstar Just Announced Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival — a One-Night Miami Launch Party on November 21
item.description: Rockstar Games has announced Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival , a one-night live music event in Miami on Saturday, November 21, 2026, to celebrate the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI . The festival…
item.content:encoded:
Rockstar Games has announced Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival, a one-night live music event in Miami on Saturday, November 21, 2026, to celebrate the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. The festival takes over Mana Wynwood, two days after the game launches on November 19, with a star-studded lineup of artists from the game and its official soundtrack — and the only way in is a ticket lottery that closes tomorrow, November 10, at 4:00 p.m. ET.

Presented by Rockstar Games and PlayStation and produced by the creators of Miami's III Points festival, the event features two stages of music spanning hip-hop, electronic, and Latin sounds — the sound of Vice City and the state of Leonida, brought to life in the city that inspired them.

The lineup

  • Cactus Jack presents Travis Scott, Don Toliver, Kodak Black, and Sofaygo
  • Cardi B
  • Metro Boomin
  • Justice (DJ set)
  • Tainy, Rauw & Friends, Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso, and Suero
  • Nick León B2B DJ Python, Prospa B2B Skream, and The Dare B2B Fcukers

How to get tickets

There is no general sale. Fans must enter a free pre-sale lottery through the official festival site, operated by Laylo and DICE. The lottery closes Tuesday, November 10, at 4:00 p.m. ET, with winners drawn at 7:00 p.m. ET. Winners can then buy tickets starting Wednesday, November 11, at 12:00 p.m. ET, first come, first served. Purchases are limited to two tickets per person, tickets are non-transferable, and attendees must be at least 17 years old.

The music does not stop at the festival. Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album arrives alongside the game on November 19 with 34 original tracks, and Grand Theft Auto VI: Original Score — 30 tracks from Justice — follows on December 11.

Rockstar has not announced a livestream, set times, or ticket prices yet. Grand Theft Auto VI launches November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. If you want to be in Miami for launch week, the clock is ticking — the lottery closes tomorrow afternoon.
